sources.title: Atsiz Garchai
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica biography of Atsiz, his Khwarazmian base, Mangyshlaq and Jand campaigns, steppe frontier, and literary court.

sources.title: The Eclipse of Khurasan in the Twelfth Century
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reassessment linking the post-1153 destruction in Khurasan to Oghuz action after Sanjar was captured.

sources.title: Malek Dinar
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica biography tracing one 1153 Oghuz chief to later rule in Kerman and its 1198 end.

sources.title: Sanjar, Ahmad b. Malekshah
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica chronology of Khwarazmian vassalage, Qatwan, the 1153 capture, escape, death, and Great Seljuk fragmentation.

sources.title: Khwarazmshahs: The Line of Anushtigin
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica synthesis used sparingly for Qutb al-Din, Atsiz, and the bounded Khwarazmian political core.

sources.title: Oghuz Revolt and the Policy Followed by Khwarezmshah Atsiz
sources.note: Peer-reviewed 2025 study of branches, named beys, sheep tribute, official abuse, battle, and Vatvat letters surrounding the 1153 revolt.

sources.title: Chashnigir, Court Food Taster
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica account of the official whose handling of the Oghuz sheep levy helped ignite the 1153 conflict.

sources.title: Il-Arslan
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica biography covering independence after Sanjar, Aytaq and Dehistan, the 1165 Khorasan campaign, and court evidence limits.

sources.title: Dehestan
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica regional history locating the 1161 Oghuz sack and later Khwarazmian campaigning.

sources.title: Balkh: History from the Arab Conquest to the Mongols
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica city history on Oghuz pasture, taxation conflict, 1152 to 1153 fighting, destruction, and temporary occupation.

sources.title: Ghaznavids
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica history noting Oghuz adventurers who held Ghazna from about 1160 for as long as fifteen years.

sources.title: Khosrow Malek
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica biography separating the last Ghaznavid ruler from Oghuz adventurers occupying Ghazna.

sources.title: Tekish b. Il-Arslan
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica chronology for Tekish, northern tribal recruitment, the 1194 defeat of the last Great Seljuk, and his death in 1200.

sources.title: Rural Dwelling in Khorezm, First to Fourteenth Centuries
sources.note: NYU-hosted 1976 archaeological monograph; chapter 3 documents twelfth to early-thirteenth-century Khwarazmian rural settlements and houses.

sources.title: On the History of the Khorezm Rural Habitation
sources.note: English article summarizing the central-corridor house form and carefully bounded hypotheses about extended family organization.

sources.title: Central Asian Architecture in the Eleventh and Twelfth Centuries: Khwarazm and Kavat-kala
sources.note: Illustrated architectural history summarizing Kavat-kala estates, mud construction, room groups, and debated towerlike outbuildings.

sources.title: Kath
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica historical geography of the Oxus, irrigation canals, fertile silt, and destructive river-course shifts in Khwarazm.

sources.title: Watwat, Rashid-al-Din
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica biography documenting madrasa education, bilingual writing, chancery work, court poetry, anecdotes, and uncertain death date.

sources.title: Vatvat qasida 141 in praise of Atsiz Khwarazmshah
sources.note: Digital Persian transcription of the exact panegyric couplet used for the written-language sample.

sources.title: Notes on Some Words Recorded as Oghuz in Divanu Lugati t-Turk
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of six lexemes explicitly marked Oghuz in the eleventh-century dialect dictionary and their later forms.

sources.title: Jorjani, Zayn-al-Din Esmail
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica biography and linguistic analysis of Jorjani, his patrons, medical encyclopedia, handbook, and Persian-Arabic terminology.

sources.title: The Treasure of Khvarazm Shah
sources.note: Library of Congress manuscript description outlining the encyclopedia’s ten parts, including hygiene, childhood, travel, treatments, and pharmacology.

sources.title: Chorasmia Medical School from the Beginning until the Mongol Invasion
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review of Gorganch, Khwarazmian patronage, physicians, and limits of reconstructing a regional medical school.

sources.title: Improvements of Kazakhstan Medieval Cities on the Great Silk Road
sources.note: Archaeological review, pages 5 to 8, of drains, soakaways, toilets, washing rooms, rubbish pits, and baths at comparison sites outside the target polygon.
